title: Clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of a vaccine for grass pollen allergy.
official: A prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous immunotherapy with polymerized grass pollen extracts in patients with grass pollen–induced allergic rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis with or without mild-to-moderate asthma
summary:
Main objective: The primary objective of this trial is to evaluate the clinical efficacy of 6-grass pollen polymerized extract, 30,000 TU/mL, and 6-grass pollen polymerized extract, 10,000 TU/mL, suspension for injection administered subcutaneously, each compared with placebo, in participants with grass pollen-induced allergic rhinitis or rhinoconjunctivitis. 
The effect will be assessed by comparing rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms and medication use between the 30,000 TU/mL group and placebo, and between the 10,000 TU/mL group and placebo, during the peak grass pollen season.
conditions: Grass pollen induced moderate-to-severe allergic rhinitis or rhinoconjunctivitis with or without mild-to-moderate asthma

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participants aged 12 to 64 years (inclusive).
2. Participants whose rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms required regular treatment with intranasal corticosteroids, with or without H1-antihistamines, during the previous grass pollen season, corresponding to an RCSMS ≥ 2 (0–6 scale), according to the scoring system described by Pfaar et al.(1)
3. Signed and dated Informed Consent Form by a legally competent participant.
4. Good general physical and mental health, as determined by the Investigator.
5. Diagnosis of grass pollen allergy, based on all of the following criteria: a.	A medical history of moderate to severe allergic rhinitis or rhinoconjunctivitis due to grass pollen allergens during at least the two previous consecutive grass pollen seasons, with clinically relevant symptoms during the grass pollen season (definition of allergy severity according to ARIA(2)), b.	Treatment with anti-allergic medication for at least 2 grass pollen seasons prior to enrolment, c.	Positive skin prick test (SPT - wheal diameter ≥5 mm) to grass pollen allergens, with a positive control (histamine) wheal ≥5 mm. The results will be valid up to 12 months prior to the signature of the informed consent.
6. Female participants: a.	Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP: a woman is considered of childbearing potential according to the CTFG, if she is fertile, following menarche and until becoming postmenopausal unless becoming permanently sterile. Permanent sterilization methods include hysterectomy, bilateral salpingectomy and bilateral oophorectomy) must be willing to use a highly effective method of contraception: i.	Oral, intravaginal or transdermal hormonal medical drugs or -devices containing estrogen/progesterone combinations. ii.	Oral, injectable or implantable hormonal medical drugs or -devices containing progesterone-only. iii.	Intrauterine device (IUD). iv.	Intrauterine hormone-releasing system (IUS). v.	Bilateral tubal occlusion. vi.	Vasectomized partner (provided, that partner is the sole sexual partner of the WOCBP trial participant and that the vasectomized partner has received medical assessment of the surgical success). b.	Women not of childbearing potential (i.e., pre-menarche, tubal ligation, hysterectomy, or post-menopausal (a postmenopausal state is defined as no menses for 12 months without an alternative medical cause),
7. For participants with asthma: a confirmed diagnosis of controlled mild-to-moderate asthma, defined for this trial as asthma requiring treatment corresponding to GINA 2026 Steps 1–3(3), with no evidence of uncontrolled or severe asthma. The diagnosis of asthma will be considered valid if established within 12 months prior to signing the informed consent form.
8. For participants with obstructive or restrictive ventilation disorders (e.g., bronchial asthma, COPD, bronchial hyperreactivity): Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1) ≥80% of the participant’s reference value or Peak Expiratory Flow (PEF) ≥80% of the participant’s individual optimal value,
9. Laboratory assessments: a.	Confirmed normal renal and liver function, including non-safety-related, non-clinically significant deviations outside the reference ranges. Participants with clinically significant deviations must be retested or excluded. Upon normalisation (being non-clinically significant) of the out-of-range value(s), the participant will be eligible.  b.	Specific IgE against grass pollen allergens or one of the components of the grass mixture (preferably Phleum pratense; e.g., Phl p 1 and/or Phl p 5) with a value ≥ 3.5 kU/L. The results will be valid for up to 12 months prior to signing the informed consent form. c.	Negative pregnancy test in blood at the screening visit for WOCBP. The pregnancy test must be confirmed by a urine test at Visit T1.
10. Participants should preferably be monosensitized to the study allergens. In the case of participants sensitized to other aeroallergens, only those with the following characteristics (results valid up to 12 months prior to signing the informed consent form) may be included in the study:  a.	Participants with a positive skin prick test for Dermatophagoides or other house dust mites. The specific IgE value for these allergens must be < 3.5 kU/L. b.	 Participants with positive skin prick test for animal dander may be included, provided that they have occasional exposure and symptoms. Participants with habitual exposure to dander or living with animals must have a negative prick test.  c.	Participants sensitized (positive skin prick test) to other pollens may only participate if their pollen season does not coincide with the observation period (O1, O2, EoT). Participants with a positive skin prick test to co-seasonal pollens must have a specific IgE value < 3.5 kU/L. d.	Participants with positive skin prick test for Alternaria alternata. The specific IgE value must be < 3.5 kU/L.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participation in another clinical trial or participation in a clinical trial within 30 days prior to enrolment,
2. Known hypersensitivity to the investigational medicinal product (IMP) excipients or placebo.
3. Uncontrolled asthma according to GINA 2026(3), including:  •	Poor symptom control (frequent symptoms, reliever use, activity limitation, or nocturnal symptoms), and/or •	Frequent exacerbations (≥2/year requiring oral corticosteroids), or •	Severe exacerbations (≥1/year requiring hospitalization).
4. FEV1 < 80% predicted or PEF < 80% of the participant’s individual optimal value despite appropriate pharmacological treatment (valid within 12 months prior to informed consent).
5. Severe asthma according to GINA 2026, or asthma requiring GINA 2026 Step 4 or Step 5 treatment.(3)
6. Present clinical symptoms of upper or lower respiratory tract infection in the last two weeks before screening visit (Scr) or first treatment visit (T1) and/or exacerbation of obstructive or restrictive ventilation disorders within 4 weeks before Scr or T1 visits.
7. Clinically significant renal or chronic hepatic disease.
8. Active malignant disease (ongoing or within the past 5 years).
9. Severe autoimmune disease.
10. Immunodeficiency, immunosuppression, or immunopathological conditions.
11. Severe uncontrolled chronic diseases (e.g., congestive heart failure, cardiovascular insufficiency, active gastric ulcer, inflammatory bowel disease, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus).
12. Previous allergen immunotherapy with grass pollen allergens within the last 5 years.
13. Any contraindication to adrenaline (epinephrine), including hyperthyroidism.
14. Active tuberculosis.
15. Known positive serology for HIV-1/2, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C.
16. Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or women of childbearing potential not using highly effective contraception.
17. Use of systemic immunosuppressive medications (e.g., methotrexate or cyclosporine A) or blood transfusion within 1 month prior to Screening.
18. Treatment with biologics (e.g., monoclonal antibodies), mast cell stabilizers, or anti-leukotriene agents.
19. Use of beta-blockers or ACE inhibitors.
20. Use of antidepressant/antipsychotic drugs with strong antihistaminic properties (e.g., tricyclic antidepressants).
21. Use of systemic or nasal corticosteroids or antihistamines within the defined wash-out period prior to Screening (except maintenance asthma treatment).
22. Missing measurement of grass pollen specific IgE.
23. Ongoing allergen immunotherapy with any allergen.
24. Sensitisation to house dust mites with specific IgE ≥ 3.5 kU/L.
25. Sensitisation to pet dander with relevant exposure.
26. Sensitisation to Alternaria alternata with specific IgE ≥ 3.5 kU/L.
27. Sensitisation to co-seasonal pollens with specific IgE ≥ 3.5 kU/L.
28. Clinically significant abnormal renal or hepatic laboratory values at Screening. Retesting is allowed once (≥7 days later); persistent abnormalities lead to exclusion.
29. Clinically relevant allergic rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis due to other environmental allergens during the observation period.
30. Any relationship of dependence with the sponsor, or Investigator.
31. Inability to understand study procedures or trial documents.
32. Participants considered unlikely to comply with the protocol (e.g., substance abuse, serious psychiatric disorders, or unwillingness to comply with study requirements).
33. Participants institutionalized by judicial or administrative order.
34. History of severe systemic allergic reactions (Grade III–IV) and/or anaphylaxis (e.g., to food, Hymenoptera venom, or medications).
